## Introduction

We are interested in adding more datasets to the Treehouse Splice Compendium prior to submitting the manuscript to a journal. Currently, the priorities are to include samples in the Treehouse PolyA compendia, with healthy comparators from dGTEx.

This notebook reads in the clinical metadata from the v25 Treehouse PolyA Compendium and filters for samples to download to process for Splice Compendium v2.
The input files to this notebook are:

polya_clinical_file: [Treehouse PolyA Compendium v25 clinical metadata](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE294351), which contains clinical (disease, age at dx, sample source) information associated with a unique th_dataset_id
treehouse_files_on_aws: An internal log of sequence files in Treehouse storage.
This file contains more files than are in the Treehouse PolyA Compendium.
Fields consist of date, time, bytes, and path.
Treehouse IDs for associating files with those in the PolyA compendium are within the values for path.

## Setup

Libraries

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```

Files and directories

```{r files_and_directories}
## Directories ##
repo_root <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::is_git_root)
metadata_dir <- file.path(repo_root, "metadata")

## Files ##
# Treehouse polyA compendium with disease type of samples and treehouse ID
polya_clinical_file <- file.path(metadata_dir, "GSE294351_clinical_Treehouse-Tumor-Compendium-25.01-PolyA_20250131v1.tsv")
# record of files on AWS, with file type information and file size.
# to be associated with polya_clinical_file by treehouse ID
treehouse_aws_summary_file <- file.path(metadata_dir, "archived_files_on_archive-treehouse-ucsc-edu_primary.txt")
```

Read in files

```{r}
## Read in files ##
polya_metadata_df <- readr::read_tsv(polya_clinical_file)

# this file is separated by spaces
treehouse_aws_df <- read.table(
  treehouse_aws_summary_file, 
  sep = "", 
  header = FALSE, 
  col.names = c(
    "date",
    "time",
    "bytes",
    "path"))
```

Summarize number of pedaya samples in polyA compendium by disease type

```{r}
polya_metadata_df |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = source_name,
                   n = dplyr::n())
```

I will exclude samples from TARGET and TCGA, since these are datasets not unique to Treehouse, TARGET is in Splice Compendium v1, and TCGA is primarily composed of adult samples.

```{r}
polya_summary_min_sample <- polya_metadata_df |>
  # filter for human pedaya samples not in TARGET and TCGA
  dplyr::filter(pedaya == "yes",
                organism == "Homo sapiens",
                ! source_name %in% c("TARGET", "TCGA")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = c(disease),
                   n = dplyr::n()) |>
  # filter for diseases with at least 15 samples to make plot readable
  dplyr::filter( n >= 15) |>
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n))

polya_summary_min_sample
```

Check how many samples in total fit these criteria

```{r}
sum(polya_summary_min_sample$n)
```

Altogether, there are \~1500 samples in the Treehouse PolyA compendium that fit these criteria. This seems like a good set to start with since it is over double the number of tumor samples currently in the splice compendium. We might want to discuss if we want to further filter out samples that are not unique to Treehouse (e.g. CBTN)

Can Treehouse polyA compendium samples of rarer diseases be grouped into larger categories? Filter for compendium samples with under 15 samples to see

```{r}
polya_summary_less_than_min_sample <- polya_metadata_df |>
  # filter for human pedaya samples not in TARGET and TCGA
  dplyr::filter(pedaya == "yes",
                organism == "Homo sapiens",
                ! source_name %in% c("TARGET", "TCGA")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = c(disease),
                   n = dplyr::n()) |>
  # filter for diseases with under 15 samples
  dplyr::filter( n < 15)

# count how many uniquely labeled disease types here have less than 15 samples
nrow(polya_summary_less_than_min_sample)
```
